tasks.short: Develop welding templates from blueprint dimensions

steps.what: Read template geometry, dimensions and tolerances from the blueprint
Choose template construction, datums and allowances
Enter and verify dimensions in the template calculation sheet
Calculate template lengths, angles and offsets
Draw the welding template in the CAD system {OTHER}
Save the template drawing in the same CAD system
Make and trial the physical template against the actual workpiece
Check dimensions and fit and correct the template

tasks.design: Test existing formula sheets and parametric template families in the CAD system {OTHER}. Verified dimensions drive arithmetic and repeat geometry, while the welder chooses allowances, edits the drawing and trials the real template; no welding machine receives commands.
tasks.previous_blocker: Blueprint interpretation and one-off template geometry were mixed with repeat arithmetic and drawing commands.
tasks.enabler_now: Native formula and parametric tools can reuse a validated family without interpreting a blueprint.
tasks.still_hard: Distortion allowances, ambiguous datums and physical access depend on the joint and workpiece.
tasks.human_edge: The welder recognises a mathematically plausible template that will not work on the bench.
tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic and repeated geometry drawing, with the same responsibility for template fit.

evidence.claim: Formula sheets and parametric CAD geometry can automate repeat template calculations and drawing commands; this is model knowledge, not a documented welding-template implementation or measured saving.

assumptions: Boundary covers template-specific geometry extraction, calculation, drawing and physical trial. General assembly and safety planning in 23611 is distinct; shared blueprint reading must be assigned once if local timings combine it.

The welder enters lengths, angles, thickness, units, datums, tolerances and chosen allowances in s3, using the engineering blueprint as source. No automatic blueprint extraction or free verified feed is assumed; unclear dimensions return to the drawing author with time retained in s1-s3.

Only fifteen current arithmetic hours are replaced. Ten of twenty CAD hours are repeated geometry commands in a compatible family; ten remain for custom features, constraint repair and drawing checks. Existing CAD runtime earns no saving.

Physical manufacture, trial and final correction stay fully retained. Ordinary one-hour drawing save has no approval gate and no saving. This design does not release production, cut metal automatically or certify a weld.
unknowns: Current template families and compatible CAD inputs
How much calculation is already automatic
Actual custom geometry and physical trial time
research_questions: Can one common template family reproduce dimensions and tolerances without manual geometry commands?
Which allowances must always be chosen by the welder?

already_counted.description: Edit and repair custom template geometry
Final physical dimensional check and correction

incremental.description: Maintain and test formulas and template families against drawing changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is fifteen arithmetic plus ten repeat-geometry hours, less three upkeep = 22. Cautious case: a one-off joint has no compatible geometry family, so all twenty drawing hours remain; only verified arithmetic removes fifteen, less three upkeep = 12. Physical template work receives no reduction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Analyze welding instructions and plan assembly operations

steps.what: Find current engineering drawings, specifications, work orders and material safety data sheets
Analyze blueprint geometry, weld specifications and material safety requirements
Inspect actual components, access and assembly conditions
Choose layout, assembly sequence and operations
Write the working layout and assembly sequence
Save the working assembly plan in the same document store

tasks.design: Configure a work-order document view in {DOCS} and reuse verified order and revision headers in the actual working plan. The welder reads original drawings and safety sheets, checks physical conditions and chooses the assembly approach; no model interprets safety instructions or controls welding.
tasks.previous_blocker: Current drawings and safety documents may be stored in separate folders with manual revision lookup.
tasks.enabler_now: Native document metadata and templates can link a work order to its controlled sources.
tasks.still_hard: Conflicting specifications, material hazards and inaccessible joints require skilled interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The welder relates written instructions to actual component fit and safe working conditions.
tasks.altitude: Slightly less document hunting and header copying; operational decisions stay with the welder.

reach.learn: Document revision control and escalation of unsafe ambiguities

evidence.claim: Controlled document links and native header templates can reduce locating and copying without interpreting welding methods; feasibility and timings are model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is planning actual assembly operations from supplied documents and physical conditions. The working assembly plan is used to lay out and sequence the job today; no new report or sign-off record is added.

Engineering supplies order ID, component IDs, document IDs, revision status, material grade and applicable safety-sheet links in the existing index. The welder verifies applicability in s1 and reads sources in s2; missing metadata or conflicting revisions require manual lookup within retained s1 time.

Three of fifteen retrieval hours are repeated folder and revision navigation; twelve remain for selecting and verifying sources. Only 0.99 of nine plan-writing hours is copying verified order and revision headers; 8.01 remains for first capture, layout choices, wording and checks.

Test native views and templates first. Ordinary same-system saving is one hour fully retained without a gate. No external send, production release or automated machine action is proposed. Template-specific dimensional extraction in 23597 must not be added again if performed during this reading.
unknowns: Whether engineering metadata is already reliable and linked
Whether an actual working plan is written for this job type
Current retrieval time versus interpretation time
research_questions: Can all current applicable source files be found from one existing work-order view?
Which plan headers are currently retyped rather than already defaulted?

already_counted.description: Verify applicable source documents and handle incomplete metadata

incremental.description: Check document links and plan headers after engineering changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Central gross is three navigation hours plus 0.99 header hours, less 0.6 upkeep = 3.39; high rounded down to 3.3. Cautious case: mixed revision metadata prevents a useful document view, so all fifteen retrieval hours remain; 0.99 header hours still fall away, less 0.6 upkeep = 0.39, rounded down to 0.3. All analysis and physical inspection stay.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The welder retains blueprint interpretation, allowances, assembly decisions and physical fit checks. Compatible template families remove some repeated calculation and drawing.
reach: Collaborate with layout workers on reusable template geometry
role.ambitious_version: A welder with reliable reusable template tools and more time for joint fit and assembly judgement.
